title: Evaluation comparison for a finite free change of ring sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Suppose that $S$, as an $R$-module sheaf, is isomorphic to $R^{\oplus d}$ for some integer $d\geq0$. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived change of rings $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], derived tensor products $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R,\otimes^{\mathbf L}_S$ (total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]), and derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], with the derived tensor–Hom adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] defining transposes. For arbitrary $P,Q\in D(R)$, the canonical morphism
$$c_{P,Q}:T H_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_S(TP,TQ)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $Q$. It is the tensor-Hom transpose of the pairing
$$TP\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T H_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(P,Q))\xrightarrow{T(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})}TQ.$$
In particular this specifies the comparison by evaluation, independently of any choice of the finite free basis. No boundedness, completeness, constructibility or perfectness hypothesis on $P$ or $Q$ is required.

proof.text: Use the existing derived change-of-rings cochain model to obtain E, T, epsilon, its universal property and computation on K-flat complexes. Use the recorded closed symmetric monoidal theorem for R and S to obtain AR, AS, MR, MS.

Apply the normalized tensor comparison theorem to those supplied models. Restore the two counit-isomorphism clauses using the cochain model computation theorem, and apply the finite-free Hom transpose theorem. Assemble exactly the same existential witnesses and normalization proofs.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q62-db2b5c011 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all cited node statements, unit sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom, the parent lem-sf-tensor-hom step 8 (which uses the item), the main-20261015 blueprint lem-sf-tensor-hom (the 'compatible with scalar extension' clause), and Stacks sites-cohomology.tex 08JA lemma-section-RHom-over-U and 08J9 lemma-internal-hom (lines 8874-8930). Compared with the base copy, the statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint fields are unchanged; only the proof, status, split_report and appended searches are new. There are no new nodes. The statement is true because S finite free over R is perfect and flat. Tested d=0, d=1, R=k with S=k[eps], and the unbounded case P = direct sum of k[n] (finite free tensor commutes with products). Step 1: the presheaf tensor with R^d is already a sheaf, the explicit inverse maps commute with d, and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings gives the K-flat computation. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction hold (small site, commutative rings, no flatness or boundedness needed); it supplies the normalized iso and conservativity of U, and it does not reach the item, so there is no cycle. Step 3: Yoneda with the Hom-adjunction from the internal-Hom node plus rhom-global-sections gives the finite product. Step 4: I re-derived the transpose. It is b_j^{P tensor H}, checkable on K-flat representatives, then by naturality of b_j it becomes b_j^Q composed with ev; the matrix entries are delta_ij. This is the specified evaluation morphism, not just some isomorphism. Step 5: conservativity, the d=0 case and basis independence are correct. Duplicate candidates checked and rejected: lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension (narrower, completed integral bounded), lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free (a different functor), lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback, lem-sf-hom-finite-projective, lem-pod-finite-projective-tensor-hom. No SGA. All seven declared tool_uses accepted as generic black-box ringed-site tools. Mathlib searches cover all three kinds (one leansearch recorded honestly as unavailable). No fixes.

      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))]
    (hfree : ∃ d : ℕ, Nonempty

        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).map φ)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit
            (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)) ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (R :=

      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max c v r}

      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)} (f : M ⟶ N),
        E.map f = eqToHom (h M) ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom φ M f ≫

        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}

        E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)

        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
      (AR : WeilConjectures.CoefficientClosedStructure
        (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R))
      (AS : WeilConjectures.CoefficientClosedStructure
        (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J S))
      (MR : WeilConjectures.CoefficientTensorModels.{r, c, v, w} J R AR)
      (MS : WeilConjectures.CoefficientTensorModels.{r, c, v, w} J S AS)
      (κ : WeilConjectures.coefficientTotalTensor.{r, c, v} J R ⋙
          E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ≅
        (E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).prod
          (E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙
            WeilConjectures.coefficientTotalTensor.{r, c, v} J S)
      (μ : AR.tensor ⋙ T ≅ T.prod T ⋙ AS.tensor)
      (α : derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R ⋙ T ≅
        T.op.prod T ⋙ derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J S),
      (∀ (P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}

        (p q : ℤ) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (P.X p).val.obj U) (y : (Q.X q).val.obj U),

            (((WeilConjectures.coefficientTotalTensor.{r, c, v} J R).obj (P, Q)).X (p + q))
            U 1 (WeilConjectures.coefficientTensorGenerator.{r, c, v} J R

        WeilConjectures.coefficientTensorGenerator.{r, c, v} J S
          ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P)
          ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Q) p q (p + q) rfl U
          (ringedFiniteFreeScalarSection.{c, v, r} J φ E h (P.X p) U 1 x)
          (ringedFiniteFreeScalarSection.{c, v, r} J φ E h (Q.X q) U 1 y)) ∧
      (∀ (P Q : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) ℤ)
        (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J) (R := R) P)

Existential E and its object/map equations specify ordinary scalar extension; T and its universal counit specify derived scalar extension. The normalized representative tensor models, pure-tensor comparison and counit square identify the strong tensor comparison, and the final equation fixes the natural Hom isomorphism as extended-evaluation transpose. No basis or condition on either derived input is chosen.
